title: Locale punctuation tokenizer aliasing - incident review
summary: During a staged rollout of model v2025-09-08b to EU regions we observed a subtle quality regression limited to locale-heavy queries. The canary looked syntactically healthy (latency, error rates) but downstream reranker/QA signals and several customer reports showed degraded ranking and repeated hallucinated entity mentions. Investigation found tokenizer symbol aliasing for several unicode punctuation codepoints introduced by a tokenizer repack step in the model build pipeline.
impact: Degradation in semantic reranking and embeddings-based similarity for ~3% of requests in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 over the canary window. No CPU/GPU resource exhaustion, p95 latency unchanged. A small set of paying customers exposed to locale-heavy prompts reported incorrect search results and increased false positive reranks.
detection: Alerting: a custom quality guardrail (rerank-ndcg-drop monitor) tripped during the canary window. Additional signals: elevated 'semantic-shift' regression metric from Optimize pipeline, two customer-support tickets, and manual QA reproductions using French and Polish corpora. Canary dashboards showed normal infra metrics which initially obscured the issue.
timeline:
2025-09-10 09:05 UTC - Canary rollout started (10% traffic eu regions)
2025-09-10 09:31 UTC - rerank-ndcg guardrail cross-threshold in eu-west-1
2025-09-10 09:40 UTC - On-call SRE alerted; quick verification of infra metrics (ok)
2025-09-10 10:02 UTC - QA reproductions confirm wrong reranks for inputs with non-ascii punctuation
2025-09-10 10:30 UTC - Investigation identifies mismatch between build-time tokenizer normalization table and runtime normalization module
2025-09-10 11:05 UTC - Decision to halt rollout and roll back to v2025-08-29-a in eu regions
2025-09-10 11:20 UTC - Rollback completed; injected tokenization normalization patch to canary staging for additional validation
2025-09-10 13:00 UTC - Post-rollback monitoring shows quality metrics back within expected bounds
2025-09-11 - Root cause analysis meeting; follow-ups assigned
root_cause: During the model repack process we applied a tokenizer serialization optimization that reordered a subset of the symbol-to-id map to compress unused codepoints. The change was intended to be neutral because we also shipped a normalization table, but a small mismatch remained: U+2019 (right single quotation mark), U+2032 (prime), and U+2009 (thin space) were normalized differently between the build artifact and the runtime normalization library used in EU-serving nodes. The mismatch produced aliasing: certain locale punctuation mapped to the wrong subtokens, producing embedding vectors that deviated enough to move examples across rerank decision boundaries. This was not caught by the standard unit tests because they used ASCII-centric test sets and the preflight validators compared only checksum of weights not tokenizer normalization semantics.
investigation_notes:
- Tokenizer binary diff shows reordering of 48 entries; 3 punctuation codepoints moved between buckets.
- Reproducer harness: sending a set of French/Polish queries with ambiguous punctuation reproduced rank flips locally when loading the new tokenizer binary.
- KV cache, batching, and runtime kernels were ruled out: logs show identical execution traces post-tokenization.
- The repacked artifact passed checksum and pragmatic metrics (perplexity) because tokenization differences manifest downstream at embedding/rerank layer not in model logits during generation tests.
- Local developer sandbox used a different locale-normalization pipeline than production-serving; this contributed to the validation gap.
immediate_mitigation:
1) Halted rollout at 10% in EU.
2) Rolled back traffic for EU regions to previous model version (v2025-08-29-a).
3) Flushed tokenizer caches and forced model hot-reloads to remove any in-memory mixed-state artifacts.
4) Deployed a temporary normalization shim to the staging canary agents to validate fixes before next rollout.
rollback_steps:
- Identify manifest of previous stable model and pin regional routing policy to that manifest.
- Invalidate CDN and tokenizer cache: SRE tooling 'cachectl invalidate --tokenizer eu-*'.
- Trigger model agent drain and restart on affected pools (controlled rolling restart).
- Confirm rerank-ndcg and semantic-shift metrics return to baseline within 60 minutes.
- Preserve logs and snapshots for forensics before tearing down crashed canary pods.
postmortem_actions:
- Add tokenizer normalization unit tests covering a representative set of unicode punctuation and locale-specific whitespace (assigned to eng-applied-ml).
- Extend preflight checks to include a deterministic tokenization equivalence test: generate token ids for a canonical multilingual probe set and assert exact match between build artifact and runtime library (assigned to release-engineering).
- Add a build-time artifact diff report that surfaces symbol reordering as a non-silent change (assigned to platform-engineering).
- Update runbook: when tokenization-related quality guardrail trips, run 'tokenizer-diff' and 'probe-similarity' steps before other mitigations (assigned to site-reliability-engineering).
- Ship a small patch to the build pipeline to lock punctuation buckets, avoid reordering, and include normalization table with the model bundle (assigned to serving-runtime).
longer_term_recommendations:
- Introduce synthetic probe monitoring in production that measures per-symbol embedding cosine similarity for a fixed multilingual probe set each deploy. This gives early detection when tokenization semantics change.
- Consider embedding-level canary tests (compute embeddings for probe set and compare embedding cosine to baseline) as part of automated rollout gating.
- Align developer sandboxes with production normalization libraries to reduce 'it works locally' gaps.
- Add a lightweight 'tokenizer manifest' file to model bundles that is validated by both build and runtime in CI.
- Review any optimizer or repacking heuristics that touch symbol tables for potential semantic impacts.
notes_to_oncall: If rerank-ndcg alert triggers again, collect tokenization-diff output immediately and add 'probe-similarity' run output to the incident channel.
Do not restart only agent processes; ensure tokenizer caches are invalidated to avoid serving mixed-state artifacts.
If rollback is needed, follow the rollback_steps above and coordinate with CS for customer communication.
